text:
maria: Heads-up 90m: TiltedLabs (pilot customer) pushed back on our default tiering. They want a hybrid: Starter baseline + per-route throughput caps + guaranteed premium lane for checkout routes. They also asked for explicit monthly "overflow" crediting in the contract. Meeting with customer success in 6h. Can we sketch options?

ton y: quick note from sales: customer won't accept user-visible regressions on checkout. They'll tolerate routing to cheaper models only for non-checkout routes. They want a conservative fallback on named routes only.

ash: from engineering POV: three feasible approaches:
- Tenant-level QoS addon (fast): increases priority across tenant, includes monthly burst tokens. No per-route enforcement.
- Named-route capacity buckets (medium): explicit per-route limits, hard caps + accounting. Requires router + billing changes.
- Soft-fallback routing (fastest): route to cheaper variant under overload, but define allowed route set (exclude checkout). Needs clear UX and metrics.

finance-bot: modeling flags: if we offer per-route buckets, pricing should be per-route per-1k RPS or per-million tokens. Burst crediting: prefer carrying unused burst forward as "credit balance" vs one-off refunds. Must model churn impact.

legal-bot: contract considerations: measurement windows (UTC month), definition of "cheaper/compatible variant" (same model family, lower quantization level), overflow credit formula, and a cap on monthly credits. Also add a clause for cross-region routing and data residency exceptions.

maria: draft product options to propose to customer: 
Option A (GA-friendly): Publish "Priority Lane" addon: tenant-level, includes X burst tokens/month, SLA uplift (on-call + alerts), priced at $Y/mo. No per-route guarantees.
Option B (pilot-specific): Named-Route Capacity: allocate N RPS or M tokens to up to 5 named routes. Includes hard caps and per-overflow credit at Z% of token rate. Engineering estimate 4-6 weeks.
Option C (conservative fallback): Customer opts into Contract Fallback for non-checkout routes: Redwood may route to compatible lower-tier variants under overload; overflow credited at a fixed rate; checkout routes excluded. Quick to ship behind flag (1-2 sprints) but has UX risk.

ash: engineering estimates: Priority Lane (2 sprints), Contract Fallback (1 sprint + QA), Named-Route Capacity (4-6 sprints). Need billing hooks + e2e tests for any crediting policy.

ton y: pricing heuristics idea: list price for Named-Route = base tier + premium multiplier for critical routes (2x). Overflow credits: cap at 20% of monthly invoice or $X, whichever lower. For pilot, offer a smaller discount for commit (e.g., 15% for 12mo).

maria: proposed pilot commitments to customer success: 
- Ship Priority Lane GA and docs before pilot starts
- Enable Contract Fallback for up to 3 named non-checkout routes with overflow credit formula and a monthly cap
- SLO alerts + dashboard for named routes
- Post-pilot decision point: build Named-Route Capacity if customer ups spend or signed 12mo commit>=$500k

legal-bot: suggested appendix language snippet: 
```
Named Route Overflow. For any Named Routes specified in the Order Form, if actual usage exceeds the allocated capacity and any monthly burst allowance, Redwood may, subject to the terms herein, route excess requests to compatible lower-performance model variants for the duration of the measured Window. In such an event, Customer shall receive an Overflow Credit equal to the lesser of (i) the credit percentage set forth in the Order Form applied to the billed token rate for overflow tokens, or (ii) the Monthly Credit Cap. Measurement Window means each UTC calendar month.
```

maria: immediate actions before CS meeting:
- @ash: one-slide tech timeline + risk bullets (EOD)
- @tony: two pricing scenarios (pilot discount vs list price) and suggested overflow cap numbers
- @legal-bot: tidy appendix language with data residency callouts
- @finance-bot: revenue model writeup for carry-forward credits vs one-off refunds

ton y: i'll lead customer call and position Priority Lane + Contract Fallback as the recommended path. If they insist on per-route buckets we escalate to roadmap commit.

ash: ok i'll prepare the tech slide.

maria: thanks all. i'll assemble the 1-pager and drop into the CS meeting thread. :rocket:
